extracted.intended_audience: comics scholars, digital humanists, and computational media researchers interested in automated analysis of comic strips
extracted.subtask_description: Applying computer-vision and distant-viewing methods (panel detection, caption/text detection, and combined analyses) to study the formal properties, caption distribution, and gag structure of newspaper comic strips, exemplified by a case study of Peanuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel detection (formal/layout analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect panel boundaries and count panel formats (e.g., one- to twelve-panel strips) to quantify formal properties and detect experiments or deviations (e.g., shifts away from a four-panel format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel detection enables distant viewing of formal trends (e.g., identifying when Schulz departs from his four-panel format). Combine panel detection with caption detection to locate text within panels and to study distributional patterns. Use panel detection outcomes to ask whether observed changes are due to authorial experimentation or other causes (e.g., health).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption/text detection (scene-text OCR approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scene text algorithms to locate textual captions in comic images, returning bounding boxes for detected text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors applied the scene text algorithms of Baek et al. (2019) as implemented in the EasyOCR Python module. This not only detects text but provides positions within panels, which allows measurement of where dialogue and captions appear (e.g., top of panel vs. bottom).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude paratext (signature/date/copyright) from caption counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove non-caption paratext (e.g., artist signatures, hand-lettered dates, copyright metadata) so counts reflect dialogue/captions only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schulz commonly signed the bottom of the last panel; to remove the signature from caption counts the authors automatically removed all text in the bottom third of the last panel. While signatures or paratext might be relevant in other studies, excluding them increases confidence that detected text is actual dialogue/caption content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual validation and sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomly sample comics for manual validation to estimate algorithm error rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors randomly selected 100 comics (434 panels) to validate caption detection. Report and inspect false positives/negatives (they reported only two false detections among 40 panels without captions and four false detections among 394 panels with captions). Manual validation helps identify typical error types and quantify performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report error modes and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Document types of detection failures and their causes (e.g., stylized lettering, exclamations, sound effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most errors arose from hard-to-detect lettering such as stylized exclamations and sound effects (e.g., 'BANG!', 'ziiiing!', 'Thump.'). Note these limits when interpreting quantitative results and consider targeted preprocessing or specialized detectors for stylized text/sfx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify caption distribution by panel position and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the presence/absence and proportion of captions across panel positions (first, middle, final) and across different total-panel formats (3-panel, 4-panel, Sundays, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from Peanuts: for four-panel dailies, textual captions occur in the first panel 98% of the time and the final panel 96% of the time; across all strips, first panels have captions at least 93% of the time. Present distributions (charts, percent tables) to reveal formal habits and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series analysis to detect stylistic change
rubrics_metrics.description: Track caption/panel metrics over time (e.g., proportion of final-panel captions by year) to identify shifts in an artist's practice or format evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors charted final-panel caption proportions by year to show that from 1956–2000 Schulz used final-panel captions over 93% on average, whereas 1950–1955 was ~85% — suggesting a style shift around 1955. Use yearly or period aggregates and highlight years dipping below thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze interplay of text and image to study gags
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how words and pictures combine to produce gags, treating the gag as a formal construct dependent on interlocking visual and textual elements across panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combined panel+caption detection to identify likely gag panels (often final panels) and measure whether gags rely more on text, image, or a mix. Ground this in theoretical definitions (Karasik & Newgarden: gag depends on the arrangement of multiple interconnection systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for format-specific conventions (daily vs. Sunday, panel counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different formats (small daily dailies vs. larger Sunday pages, varying panel counts) have distinct design constraints and conventions that affect caption usage and gag types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., three- and four-panel dailies showed high caption rates in first/last panels, while Sunday and >4-panel strips were more likely to feature nonverbal gags. Interpret findings relative to format constraints and newspaper editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize quantitative findings with close reading and historical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine distant-viewing quantitative results with close-reading, interviews, and historical scholarship to interpret causes (e.g., production conditions, career milestones, health) behind stylistic patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors discuss Schulz's own account of evolving from magazine-style gag cartoons to longer narratives, UFS contract milestones (paper counts), and possible impact of his essential tremor. Use archival and secondary sources to explain trends revealed computationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use computational results as baseline comparators for future studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat findings from one corpus (e.g., Peanuts) as a baseline (e.g., 'Schulzian Symmetry') against which to compare other strips or creators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors propose applying the methods to Luann, Cathy, Curtis, Jumpstart, and to strips by women and creators of color to see alignment or deviation from Schulz's symmetry. Design comparative studies using the same detection pipelines and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance and corpus collection transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the source, scraping method, and metadata provenance for the comic corpus used in analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors collected Peanuts strips from GoComics.com using a web scraper and included associated metadata. Provide DOI or data repository (they provide https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/5H0NCA) and cite ethical/legal considerations when scraping publisher-controlled content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extendable feature analyses for richer formal study
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond panels and captions, plan analyses of additional formal features such as linework, textures, character recognition, and representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors suggest future work applying distant viewing to linework, textures, and character recognition. Use suitable computer-vision models and consider multimodal feature fusion for richer interpretation of comics aesthetics and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and operationalize domain concepts (e.g., 'Schulzian Symmetry', 'gag')
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear working definitions for theoretical constructs used as evaluation axes, and operationalize them into measurable features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper defines 'Schulzian Symmetry' as the unity of uniform panel formula, consistent caption placement, and narrative cohesion between opening and closing panels. For operationalization, measure uniformity of panel counts, caption placement frequency (top), and cohesion metrics (caption presence in first+last panels).
